questions.q: When is a synchronous call a better choice than publishing an event?
o: When the caller needs the answer right now, such as a balance query
When many services must react to a change later
When the receiver may be offline for hours
When the sender should never wait
questions.w: Events suit work that can happen later and reactions by several parties. A query needing an immediate result is a synchronous call, protected by timeouts.

questions.q: What does an API gateway typically do?
o: Routes requests and handles authentication and rate limiting
Stores all business data for the services
Replaces every service-to-service call with events
Runs the business rules of each service
questions.w: It keeps services private and simpler. Business logic does not belong in the gateway, or it becomes a bottleneck and a new monolith.

questions.q: Why use a backend for frontend instead of one generic API?
o: Each client type gets responses shaped for it, owned by its own team
It removes the need for authentication
It makes all clients use the same payloads
It replaces the services behind it
questions.w: A mobile BFF can return small combined responses while a web BFF returns richer data, without bending the shared services.

questions.q: Which change to a JSON API is backward compatible?
o: Adding an optional field to a response
Renaming an existing field
Changing a number field to a string
Making an optional request field required
questions.w: Old callers ignore fields they do not know, provided they are tolerant readers. Removals, renames and type changes break callers.

questions.q: What does a consumer-driven contract test (Pact) give you?
o: The provider's build fails if a change would break what a consumer relies on
A full end-to-end test of all services at once
Automatic generation of the provider's business logic
A replacement for versioning and deprecation
questions.w: Consumers record their expectations and the provider verifies them in CI, catching breaking changes before release.

questions.q: When would you pick gRPC over REST?
o: For fast internal calls that need a strict typed contract and streaming
For public APIs that browsers call directly
When responses must be easy to cache by HTTP caches
When clients must read payloads in a text editor
questions.w: gRPC generates typed code from a .proto file and uses compact Protobuf over HTTP/2. REST suits public APIs and browsers.

questions.q: What is the standard format for returning HTTP API errors in Spring?
o: Problem Details (RFC 9457) with a type and status
A plain text message that includes the stack trace
An HTML error page shown to every client
A custom XML body that differs for each endpoint
questions.w: Spring supports it as ProblemDetail. Add a machine-readable code and correlation id, and keep stack traces in the log.

questions.q: How does a caller find instances of a service on Kubernetes?
o: Through a Service with a stable DNS name
By hard-coding the current IP address of each pod
By asking the API gateway for pod addresses
By reading the node filesystem for addresses
questions.w: The platform tracks ready pods behind the Service, so a separate registry is rarely needed.
